```{r load}
library(rcpgsd)
```

This vignette describes two further features of `rcpgsd`: consistency thresholds adjusted for early efficacy stopping, and simulation to check the closed-form results. The notation follows the vignette "Regional consistency probability under group sequential designs".

## Null RCP under a group sequential design

Homma (2026) showed that, with multiple primary endpoints, the Bonferroni-adjusted critical value selects more extreme overall estimates and thereby inflates the RCP under the null hypothesis (the null RCP) when the consistency thresholds of a single endpoint are used. Early efficacy stopping in a group sequential design has the same effect: at an early analysis the efficacy boundary exceeds the fixed-design critical value, and the RCP given stopping there is larger than in the fixed design even when the treatment has no effect.

The function `rcpgsd_get_gamma()` computes the null RCP given efficacy stopping at each analysis. As reference it uses the null RCP of the fixed design with the same final number of events and regional proportions. It then finds, for each analysis, the threshold that restores the null RCP to this reference value. The Method 1 thresholds depend on the numbers of events only through the information fractions. A positive Method 2 threshold applies only to the numbers of events supplied, because, with the default `gamma_M2 = 0`, doubling all of them divides the adjusted Method 2 thresholds by $\sqrt{2}$.

```{r gamma}
design <- list(upper = c(3.7103, 2.5114, 1.9930), alpha = 0.025)
adj <- rcpgsd_get_gamma(design, events = c(262, 523, 785),
                        fs = c(0.10, 0.45, 0.45))
adj
```

For Method 1, the null RCP given stopping at the first analysis is `r sprintf("%.3f", adj$result$rcp0_M1_unadj[1])` with the unadjusted threshold, against a fixed-design reference of `r sprintf("%.3f", adj$ref[["M1"]])`; the adjusted threshold at that analysis is `r sprintf("%.3f", adj$result$gamma_M1_adj[1])`.

```{r gamma-plot}
plot(adj)
```

At the final analysis the null RCP with the unadjusted threshold can be slightly below the reference value. By default (`allow_relax = FALSE`) the unadjusted threshold is then kept, so that thresholds are only made stricter. With `type = "overall"`, a single threshold common to all analyses is obtained so that the overall null RCP given success equals the reference value.

```{r gamma-overall}
adj_ov <- rcpgsd_get_gamma(design, events = c(262, 523, 785),
                           fs = c(0.10, 0.45, 0.45), type = "overall")
adj_ov$result[, c("stage", "gamma_M1_adj", "gamma_M2_adj")]
adj_ov$overall
```

## RCP under the alternative with adjusted thresholds

The adjusted thresholds are passed to `rcpgsd()` as analysis-specific thresholds.

```{r alternative}
res_adj <- rcpgsd(design, events = c(262, 523, 785),
                  fs = c(0.10, 0.45, 0.45), hr = exp(-0.2),
                  gamma_M1 = adj$result$gamma_M1_adj,
                  gamma_M2 = adj$result$gamma_M2_adj)
res_unadj <- rcpgsd(design, events = c(262, 523, 785),
                    fs = c(0.10, 0.45, 0.45), hr = exp(-0.2))
cbind(res_unadj$overall[, c("method", "rcp")],
      rcp_adjusted = res_adj$overall$rcp)
```

## Checking the numerical evaluation

With `approach = "simulation"`, `rcpgsd()` simulates the same normal model that underlies the closed form. Agreement between the two confirms the numerical evaluation of the multivariate normal probabilities and of the integral used on the hazard reduction scale.

```{r normal-sim}
res_cf  <- rcpgsd(design, events = c(150, 300, 450),
                  fs = c(0.10, 0.45, 0.45), hr = 0.72, scale = "hr")
res_sim <- rcpgsd(design, events = c(150, 300, 450),
                  fs = c(0.10, 0.45, 0.45), hr = 0.72, scale = "hr",
                  approach = "simulation", nsim = 100000, seed = 1)
cbind(res_cf$stage[, c("method", "stage")],
      closed_form = res_cf$stage$rcp, simulation = res_sim$stage$rcp)
```

## Patient-level simulation

The closed form relies on the normal approximation of the regional log hazard ratio estimates, which may be inaccurate when the region of interest has few events. The function `rcpgsd_sim()` simulates event-driven trials at the patient level:

- patients enter by piecewise uniform accrual, specified by region and accrual interval;
- event times are exponential, and patients may drop out at exponential times (argument `lambda_d`, no drop-out by default);
- analysis $k$ takes place when the cumulative number of observed events reaches `events[k]`;
- the boundaries are applied to the log-rank statistic, and the hazard ratios in the overall population and in each region are estimated by the same method: Cox regression (`estimator = "cox"`, default), or the method of Peto or Pike (`"peto"`, `"pike"`); the regional estimates use the data of that region only.

In the following example, 600 patients enter over 18 months and Japan starts enrolling after month 6. The number of simulated trials is kept small here to limit the run time; at least 10,000 trials are advisable in practice.

```{r patient-sim}
n_acc <- rbind(c(0, 60),      # region 1 (Japan): months 0-6, 6-18
               c(100, 170),   # region 2
               c(100, 170))   # region 3
sim <- rcpgsd_sim(design, events = c(150, 300, 450), hr = 0.72,
                  lambda_c = log(2) / 12, accrual_time = c(0, 6, 18),
                  n_accrual = n_acc, nsim = 1000, seed = 1)
sim
```

The mean regional event proportions `sim$fs_mean` reflect the delayed enrolment in Japan. Passing them to `rcpgsd()` gives the closed-form results for the same trial, which can be compared with the simulation together with the Monte Carlo standard error.

```{r compare}
cf <- rcpgsd(design, events = c(150, 300, 450), fs = sim$fs_mean,
             hr = 0.72)
cbind(sim$stage[, c("method", "stage")],
      closed_form = cf$stage$rcp,
      simulation  = sim$stage$rcp,
      mc_se       = sim$stage$se_rcp)
```

The columns `p_no_est_r1` and `p_inf_r1` of `sim$analysis` give the proportions of simulated trials in which no Japanese estimate was available or in which it was infinite (for the Cox estimate, all Japanese events observed while both groups were at risk occurred in one group). These cases indicate where the normal approximation is least reliable.

```{r analysis}
sim$analysis
```

## References

Homma G (2026). A cautionary note on regional consistency evaluation with multiple primary endpoints in multiregional clinical trials. *Pharmaceutical Statistics*, 25, e70111.
